sections.content:
In Spanish, we use **alguien** (someone, anyone) and **nadie** (no one, nobody) when referring to unspecified people.

• **Double Negation Rule**: When *nadie* comes *after* the verb, you **must** place **no** before the verb:
  *No vino nadie a la fiesta.*
• When *nadie* comes *before* the verb, do **not** use *no*:
  *Nadie vino a la fiesta.*

sections.title: Rules and Patterns
rows: No vi a nadie en la calle.

items.spanish: No escuché a nadie llamar a la puerta.
items.english: I didn't hear anyone knock on the door.

sections.content: Remember: Spanish loves double negatives! *No vino nadie* is completely grammatical and standard.
